topic.title: Analysing experimental data: accuracy, reliability, validity, anomalies and graphs
topic.subject: science
topic.examWeightHint: Unit 7 is a quarter of the award. Every Booklet A task processes its own readings (a mean, a worked-out column, a rate or a speed to the stated places) and most set a graph; every Booklet B paper has a five-mark graph (scale, label, points, line) and often a gradient with its unit, a total read from a curve or an anomaly left out of a mean.
mustMemorise: Record readings to the places the table asks for; the unit goes in the heading, quantity / unit
Leave an anomalous reading out of the mean, and divide by the number of readings kept
Extension = stretched length − unstretched length; rate = 1 ÷ time; average speed = distance ÷ time
A scale must be linear and cover at least half of each axis; each axis label is the column heading
Physics and Chemistry: one straight line or smooth curve of best fit; Biology: point to point only when the question says so
The total volume of gas is the level part of the curve, never the readings added up
Gradient = rise ÷ run from a large triangle; its unit is the y unit per x unit
The gradient of force against extension is the spring constant k; of voltage against current, the resistance R
notOnThisSpec: Error bars, uncertainty and the uncertainty of a gradient
Lines of best fit worked out by calculation (least squares) rather than drawn by eye

note.title: Analysing experimental data
note.subject: science

mustKnow: gradient = rise ÷ run, in y-axis unit per x-axis unit
F = ke, so k is the gradient of force against extension
R = V ÷ I, so R is the gradient of voltage against current

notOnThisSpec: Error bars and the uncertainty of a gradient
Lines of best fit found by calculation

mustBeAbleTo: Record readings to the stated places, with units in the headings and a mean column
Spot an anomalous reading, leave it out and average the rest with the sum in brackets
Work out a new column: extension by subtracting, rate as 1 ÷ time, speed as distance ÷ time
Choose a linear scale that fills at least half of each axis, and label each axis quantity / unit
Plot to within half a small square and draw the right line: best fit in Physics and Chemistry, point to point in Biology when asked
Read a total from the level part of a curve and the time the reaction stopped
Find a gradient from a large triangle, give its unit and say what it means
Tell accuracy, reliability and validity apart and say what improves each
sheet.howExamined: Booklet A is three practical tasks done in school, 15 marks each; after the readings come the processing marks: a mean, a worked-out column, a rate or a speed to the stated places, and often a graph of a printed data set. Booklet B is three 30-minute written papers of 35 marks: nearly every paper has a five-mark graph (the scale, the label with its unit, the points and the line), and many add a gradient with its unit, a total read from a curve, a value read from the line or an anomaly to leave out before averaging.
traps: The x-axis label left off, and the total volume of gas found by adding every reading in the table instead of reading the level part of the curve (Summer 2025 Booklet B Chemistry Higher Q2 and Foundation Q2)
An anomalous reading kept in the average, losing both marks (Summer 2024 Booklet B Physics Higher Q2 and Foundation Q4)
A non-linear scale on a circuit graph, and the voltmeter placed in series (Summer 2024 Booklet B Physics Higher Q3)
An axis without its label, a scale whose equal distances do not mean equal steps, and a curve ruled from point to point (Summer 2023 Booklet B Physics Higher Q4)
The gradient worked out, but its unit wrong (Summer 2025 Booklet B Physics Higher Q3)
Concentration written on the axis without its unit (Summer 2023 Booklet B Chemistry Higher Q3)
Rates not recorded to the four decimal places asked for (Summer 2023 Booklet A Chemistry Higher Q1)
A ruled straight line or point-to-point line where a curve was needed, or a bar chart drawn instead (Summer 2023 Booklet B Chemistry Foundation Q3)
Not saying the distance and time are measured before the speed is calculated, and ignoring the bold instruction to give 1 decimal place (Summer 2023 Booklet B Physics Higher Q3)
Readings not to the decimal places asked, V ÷ I worked wrongly on the calculator, and voltage given as the independent variable when the current was set (Summer 2023 Booklet A Physics Foundation Q1)
Hooke's law not recalled, and very few using the word subtract to find an extension (Summer 2024 Booklet B Physics Foundation Q1)
The dependent variable not named exactly as the compressed length, and the unit of k not known (Summer 2024 Booklet B Physics Higher Q4)
The unit left out of the axis label; the column heading should be the axis label word for word (Summer 2025 Booklet A Physics Foundation Q1)

workedExamples.stem:
A student hangs weights on a spring whose unstretched length is 7.5 cm.
Force / N: 1.2, 2.4, 3.6, 4.8
Length / cm: 9.5, 11.5, 13.5, 15.5
Find the extension for the 4.8 N weight. A graph of force (up the side) against extension (across) is a straight line through the origin. Use it to find the spring constant, give its unit and say what it means. [6]

steps.decision: Subtract the unstretched length: the length itself is not the extension.

steps.working: Two points far apart on the line: (0, 0) and (8.0 cm, 4.8 N), so the rise is 4.8 N
steps.decision: A large triangle, from points on the line itself.

options: F = ke, so force ÷ extension is k, and that is what the gradient measures
The gradient of any spring graph is 1
The gradient is the extension for each newton
whyMenu.explain: With force up the side and extension across, rise ÷ run is F ÷ e, which Hooke's law says is k. Swap the axes and the gradient would be 1 ÷ k.

steps.decision: The y-axis unit per the x-axis unit.

steps.working: k = 0.6 N/cm: the force needed to stretch the spring by 1 cm
steps.decision: Say what the number stands for.

options.text: the force needed for each centimetre of extension
options.feedback: Newtons per centimetre: force for each cm of stretch.
That is 1 ÷ k, the axes read the other way round.
The gradient is about how the force changes with the extension, not the length.

workedExamples.finalAnswer: k = 0.6 N/cm, the force for each centimetre of extension

twin.stem: A spring 10.0 cm long unstretched is 12.5 cm long when a 2.0 N weight hangs on it, and it obeys Hooke's law. Find its spring constant and give its unit.

workedExamples.stem:
Readings for a length of wire (current, voltage): 0.10 A, 1.1 V; 0.20 A, 2.2 V; 0.30 A, 3.3 V; 0.40 A, 4.4 V; 0.50 A, 5.5 V.
The graph of voltage (up the side) against current (across) is a straight line through the origin. Calculate the gradient of the line and state its unit. [4]

steps.working: Two points far apart on the line: (0, 0) and (0.50 A, 5.5 V). Rise = 5.5 V
steps.decision: Gradient = rise ÷ run: the equation first, from points on the line.
The run is the change across, in amps.

options: V = IR, so voltage ÷ current is the resistance: the gradient of this graph
The gradient is the current for each volt
The gradient is always the largest voltage
whyMenu.explain: With voltage up the side and current across, rise ÷ run is V ÷ I, the resistance. A straight line through the origin means the resistance stays the same.

steps.decision: The y unit per the x unit: V/A, which is the ohm.

twin.stem: Readings for another wire (current, voltage): 0.05 A, 0.7 V; 0.10 A, 1.4 V; 0.15 A, 2.1 V; 0.20 A, 2.8 V; 0.25 A, 3.5 V. The graph of voltage against current is a straight line through the origin. Calculate its gradient and state its unit.

workedExamples.stem:
The graph shows the volume of gas given off when marble chips react with dilute hydrochloric acid.
Use the graph to find the total volume of gas and the time at which the reaction stopped. Then calculate the rate = 1 ÷ time for the reaction. Give the rate to 4 decimal places, with its unit. [4]

findTheMistake.stem:
Aoife is asked: 'Four readings of the focal length of a lens are 247 mm, 253 mm, 250 mm, 206 mm. Calculate the most reliable value of the focal length. [2]'
Her answer:
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: 206 mm is far from the other three, which agree to within 6 mm, so it is anomalous and must be left out. The mean of the other three is (247 + 253 + 250) ÷ 3 = 250 mm.
findTheMistake.feedback: No marks: the anomaly is in the mean, so neither the sum nor the value earns. Summer 2024 Booklet B examiners saw a substantial number lose both marks this way.

findTheMistake.stem:
Sam is asked: 'Gas volumes read every 20 s are 0, 21, 33, 39, 41, 42, 42 cm³. What is the total volume of gas given off? [1]'
His answer:
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: Each reading is the total volume so far, not a new amount, so adding them counts the same gas again and again. The readings level off at 42 cm³, and that is the total.
findTheMistake.feedback: No marks. Summer 2025 Booklet B examiners saw many add up every reading in the table.

findTheMistake.stem:
Ciara is asked: 'A graph of resistance / Ω against length / m for a wire is a straight line through the origin. Use the triangle shown (rise 6.4 Ω, run 0.40 m) to find the gradient, and give its unit. [4]'
Her answer:
findTheMistake.whatWentWrong: The working and the value are right. A gradient's unit is the y-axis unit per the x-axis unit, so here it is ohms per metre, Ω/m, not the y unit alone.
findTheMistake.feedback: Three marks of four: only the unit's mark is lost. Summer 2025 Booklet B examiners found the gradient's unit defeated a surprising number.

findings.asked: Plot a volume-time graph and read the total volume of gas from it.
findings.wentWrong: The x-axis label was the usual lost mark; many read the total by adding every value in the table instead of from the flat part of the curve.
findings.rule: Both axes labelled with quantity and unit; totals come from the plateau.

findings.asked: Calculate an average from repeated readings, one of which is anomalous.
findings.wentWrong: A substantial number included the anomalous reading in the average and lost both marks.
findings.rule: Circle the anomaly, leave it out, then average.

findings.asked: Plot a graph from circuit readings.
findings.wentWrong: Well plotted, but a small minority chose a non-linear scale.
findings.rule: Equal distances on an axis mean equal steps in the quantity.

findings.asked: Plot a current-voltage graph for a lamp.
findings.wentWrong: Axis labels were missed by a few, unsuitable scales by the least able, and some ruled straight lines from point to point instead of drawing a curve.
findings.rule: Best-fit line or smooth curve - never dot-to-dot.

findings.asked: Measure a drawn cell and its nucleus against a scale, then give the ratio of the two diameters.
findings.wentWrong: The measuring was mostly right, but fewer gave the ratio correctly: many wrote it the wrong way round.
findings.rule: Write a ratio in the order the question names the two quantities.

findings.asked: Plot resistance against length of wire, find the gradient and its unit.
findings.wentWrong: The graph was excellent apart from the odd missing label or unit; the gradient was calculated, but its unit defeated a surprising number.
findings.rule: Gradient unit = y-axis unit per x-axis unit (ohms per cm).

insight.ruleToRemember: Label both axes with quantity and unit (matching the table headings), choose linear scales that use most of the grid, plot accurately, then draw a straight line or smooth curve of best fit - never join the dots. Spot and exclude anomalies before averaging, read values from the line, give ratios in the order asked, and give a gradient its unit.
insight.aStarSignal: A graph that needs no correction, an anomaly handled and explained, and a gradient with its unit and physical meaning.
